newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SOCCER-JAPAN KEEP ALIVE ASIAN BID FOR YOUTH TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JAPAN KEEP ALIVE ASIAN BID FOR YOUTH TITLE.

text.p: Japan kept alive Asia's dwindling challenge at the world youth soccer championship when they drew 3-3 with Paraguay on Monday to reach the knockout stage.
Japan, who finished runners-up in group D, now face a second-round clash with Australia, who beat defending champions Argentina 4-2 after Kosta Salapasidis scored all the goals.
The Japanese led 3-2 after an hour through goals from Jojo in the 31st minute, Hiroyama (45th) and Yanagisawa (60th), but Samdio equalised for Paraguay with 15 minutes left.
At the start of the day it had looked as if Japan would be the only Asian side progressing.
China and South Korea both failed to live up to their pre-tournament promise, while Malaysia and the United Arab Emirates seemed out of their depth.
However, the Emirates stunned favoured Ivory Coast 2-0 on a day of surprise results to enter the second round.

"It was a good result for us today," said Japan's coach Masakumi Tamamoto. "We only gained one point but now we have to think about our next game. We're still a young team so now we must go and plan for the next match."
Japan have conceded seven goals in their opening three matches but the coach is not too worried about his defence, which the physical Australians will put to the test on Thursday.

"When we were putting this team together we thought about taking it to world-class level," he said. "To do that, it's important to control a game so I placed importance on good midfield players. If we lose some goals it's okay, if we can score more than the opponents."
In group F, England finished top on maximum points after beating Mexico 1-0, Michael Owen hitting the winner in the 65th minute.
England will play Argentina in what is expected to be the top clash of the second round.
Argentina's defeat means the defending champions are in the same half of the draw as Brazil, who headed group C and have looked to be the dominant side of the tournament.
